:::{#sol-prereq-composition}

1. $f(g(2)) = 11$ and $g(f(2)) = 25$.
   First, $g(2) = 4$, so $f(g(2)) = f(4) = 3 \cdot 4 - 1 = 11$.
   Second, $f(2) = 5$, so $g(f(2)) = g(5) = 25$.
   The two orders give different values.
2. $f(g(x)) = f\paren{x^2} = 3x^2 - 1$.

The course writes $f(g(x))$ as $(f \circ g)(x)$ and uses composition throughout.
To review, read @def-composition.

:::
